messages:
jordan: heads up — after the kernel/driver canary pushed to eu-west-gpu, we're seeing NVLink/P2P disappear on Ampere nodes. throughput dropped ~40% on some pods.

marta: seeing same in canary-gpu-2. nv_peer_mem init shows lots of mapping failures. nvidia-smi topo -m reports all GPUs as "!=" (no P2P). :eyes:

kai: deploy-bot shows kernel 6.0.14 rolled at 14:03 UTC to eu-west-gpu-pool. Did we also bump the nvidia driver to 535?

deploy-bot: kernel-rollout: kernel=6.0.14 deployed to group=eu-west-gpu-pool at=2026-11-28T14:03:12Z by=eng-infra-canary. driver-upgrade=535.86 queued.

ada: quick log snippet from host gpu-12: 
```
[  123.456789] nvidia: nvlink: hostmem_map failed: -22
[  123.456800] nvidia: p2p_bar1_map: BAR1 size 0x0, required >=0x80000000
[  123.456810] pcieport 0000:00:1c.0: ACS: Ingress/egress rules enforced
```

marta: that p2p_bar1_map line looks like BAR1 sizing got unset by the driver+kernel combo. BAR1 size 0x0 means no aperture exposed for P2P, so peer mappings fail.

jordan: could be the PCIe ACS change in kernel 6.0 that tightened isolation by default on our Ampere PCIe switches. When ACS blocks, BAR1 peer access can't be established.

kai: confirmed with lspci -vvv on affected host — bridge shows "ACS enabled" and downstream ports have "ACS: p2plk" flags.

marta: temporary mitigation idea: revert kernel on canary or pin driver version back to 525 series. Also we can test explicit override of BAR1 via nvidia kernel module params? anyone tried nvidia NV_P2P configs?

ada: tried forcing driver param `NVreg_EnablePCIeGen3=1` — no luck. BAR1 still 0. Suspect the kernel's PCI subsystem refuses to allocate large BAR windows when ACS policy rejects cross-device BAR1 mappings.

jordan: ops recommendation: pause further kernel/driver rollouts in eu-west, open a bisection task to determine whether kernel or driver is primary cause. If it's kernel ACS change we may need a kernel cmdline flag or backport a patch.

kai: opening an incident ticket and marking Dedicated capacity nodes as degraded. CDN jobs that rely on GPU P2P for multi-GPU batching will be impacted. Cost will go up if we fall back to multi-process copies.

marta: short triage notes for the ticket: reproduce steps, sample host logs above, nvidia-smi topo -m outputs, lspci -vvv section, and list of node IDs. Also add perf numbers comparing before/after for a common microbenchmark (tensor-copy latency).

ada: workaround we validated on one node: rollback kernel to 5.15.0 and keep driver 535 — P2P returned immediately. So either kernel change in 6.x or interaction with 535 driver causes BAR1 to be zeroed.

jordan: OK let's: 1) pause rollout, 2) rollback canary to 5.15 for now, 3) start driver/kernel bisection in parallel, 4) notify product about potential throughput/regression and ETA for mitigation.

deploy-bot: rollback-start: target=eu-west-gpu-canary, action=kernel-revert->5.15.24 at=2026-11-28T14:18:00Z initiated-by=jordan

kai: assigning bisection to @marta and @ada. I'll schedule a quick all-hands sync if we need cross-team support.

marta: will capture a minimal repro and try pairing 5.15+535, 6.0+525, 6.0+535 to pinpoint combo.

jordan: thanks. tagging infra-cost: we should track any increased egress/copy cost while this is mitigated.

ada: noted. adding perf impact to incident ticket.

kai: any chance this is specific to Ampere/NVLink topology? other node types (V100) report OK.

marta: looks Ampere-specific — the BAR1 mapping behavior is different on A100 hardware; will include hardware model matrix in the ticket.

jordan: good progress. keep thread updated with bisection results. :thumbsup:
